newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-TOP SEED AUDINA CRASHES TO EARTH.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-TOP SEED AUDINA CRASHES TO EARTH.

text.p: BIRMINGHAM, England, March 12 - Mia Audina's hopes of becoming the youngest women's All England badminton winner were dashed on Wednesday.

The 17-year-old Indonesian top seed looked to be on course for the quarter-finals when she took the first game from unseeded Dai Yun 11-6 but the Chinese never gave up the battle and eventually wore down her opponent to win 6-11 11-8 11-5.
It was a big setback for Audina who has been a force in world badminton since she was 14.
After her defeat Indonesian coach Retno Kustyah said: "The Chinese always play harder against Mia because she's the one they really want to beat. She was always in a tough part of the draw."
Audina will now head home for training before returning to Europe in time for the world championships in Scotland in May when she hopes to retrieve her winning ways.
World champion Heryanto Arbi returned to something like his best form following injury which has seen him drop down the world rankings.

Seeded only joint ninth, he swept into a 10-0 lead in the first game against number two seed Rashid Sidek of Malaysia, the man who finished runner-up here last year to Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen.

Arbi, producing the kind of dazzling smashes that brought him two All England titles earlier in his career, appeared in good trim and eventually won 15-7 15-8 to claim his place in the quarter-finals starting on Thursday.
Arbi's display was in some contrast to his second-round match where he had a scare before finally quelling 20-year-old Mark Constable of England 10-15 15-10 15-9.
Former world champion Joko Suprianto, also from Indonesia, went out in the second round to Peter Rasmussen, the Dane winning comfortably 15-10 15-3.
His departure followed that of two other top compatriots, Allan Budi Kusuma and Ardy Wiranata, the gold and silver medal winners of the Barcelona Olympics in 1992.
Meanwhile, the Atlanta Olympics gold medallist Hoyer-Larsen was making unruffled progress, having reached the third round with a 15-2 15-8 defeat of China's Xie Yang Chun.
